subject: Remove the default "completion" cmd if it is alone (#1559)

agent.tail:
nce:Now I understand the mechanics. Let me trace the test requirements:

- `initCompleteCmd` adds `__complete` only when `args[0]` resolves to it; otherwise removes it.
- `InitDefaultCompletionCmd` must take `args ...string`, and when the program has no *real* sub-commands (excluding the auto-added `__complete`/`help`), only keep the `completion` command if `Find(args)` resolves to `completion`, or to `__complete` with `completion` as its first arg (i.e. `prog __complete completion <TAB>`).

Two changes needed:

1. **`command.go`** — `ExecuteC` must compute `args` and run `initCompleteCmd(args)` *before* `InitDefaultCompletionCmd(args...)`. `InitDefaultHelpCmd` stays first so `__complete` alone doesn't trigger help-command creation on subcommand-less programs.Now update `InitDefaultCompletionCmd` in completions.go:Now add the conditional removal after `c.AddCommand(completionCmd)`:Now let me build and run the target test:Target test passes. Now run the full suite to check for regressions:Some tests failed. Let me look at the failures:One failure: `TestCompleteCompletion`. Let me look at it:The test distinguishes `prog __complete completion` (completing the word "completion" — must NOT offer it, since the program has no subcommands) from `prog __complete completion ""` (completing *into* the completion command — must keep it). So the keep-condition needs `len(compArgs) > 1`, not `> 0`:All tests pass now. Let me run the full suite including sub-packages:All green. Let me review the final diff:Done. The target test passes and the full suite (`go test ./...`) is clean with no regressions.

## Changes

**`command.go`** — `ExecuteC`: moved `args` computation and `initCompleteCmd(args)` ahead of `InitDefaultCompletionCmd(args...)`, which now receives the program arguments. `InitDefaultHelpCmd` still runs first so the presence of `__complete` alone can't trigger help-command creation on subcommand-less programs.

**`completions.go`** — `InitDefaultCompletionCmd(args ...string)`:
- Dropped the `!c.HasSubCommands()` early return; instead it detects "real" program sub-commands, excluding Cobra's own `__complete` (`ShellCompRequestCmd`) and `help` (`c.helpCommand`) commands.
- The `completion` command is added, then — mirroring `initCompleteCmd`'s pattern — removed via `Find(args)` when it would be the program's only sub-command, unless:
  - `Find` resolves to `completion` itself (`prog completion`), or
  - `Find` resolves to `__complete`/`__completeNoDesc` with `completion` as the first arg and more args after it (`prog __complete completion <TAB>` — so completing *into* the command still lists `bash`/`zsh`/`fish`/`powershell`, while `prog __complete completion` does not offer `completion` as a candidate).

This preserves the new capability the commit wants — `__complete` on a subcommand-less root now reaches `getCompletions` with only `__complete` present, so its `len(rootCmd.Commands()) == 1` removal still lets the root command accept/complete arguments.
